Alchemist Distance Learning

Source: vignettes/alchemist-distance-learning.Rmd
alchemist-distance-learning.Rmd

Alchemist replaces empirical Gower-distance tuning with a supervised distance learner. It starts from a prepared Candidates object, builds pairwise trait features between candidate models, and trains a learner to predict transfer error. The learned distance matrix is then used by ordination, admissibility review, benchmarking, and policy recommendation.

Use this path when you have enough anchor diversity to learn how trait differences map to acoustic-transfer error. When anchors are sparse, the empirical similarity path is usually easier to diagnose because its parameters remain direct weights and kernel settings.

cfg <- create_configuration_template()

cfg$alchemist <- list(
  taxonomic_distance = TRUE,
  feature_type = "difference",
  distill_workers = 4,
  learner = list(
    methods = c("glm_elastic", "mars", "rf"),
    inner_folds = 3,
    workers = 4,
    seed = 20260702,
    outcome_transform = "log1p",
    lambda_rule = "lambda.1se"
  )
)

config <- build_configurer(cfg)
candidates <- build_candidates(config)
alchemist <- as_alchemist(candidates, config = config)
alchemist <- forge_distances(alchemist)

The alchemist section owns this path. similarity still matters because it defines the candidate traits and coherence features available to the learner, but empirical tuning controls in tuning do not control Alchemist fitting.

Key parameterization choices:

  • taxonomic_distance: collapses family/genus/species distance into one continuous taxonomic feature when possible.
  • feature_type: choose difference when signed standardized differences are meaningful; choose gower for bounded unsigned distances.
  • learner.methods: use a small, defensible learner library before expanding to heavier models.
  • learner.inner_folds: keep folds low when pair tables are small; larger values are useful only when anchor support is broad.
  • distill_workers: controls trait-dropout sensitivity parallelism, not the main learner fit.

Alchemist diagnostics should focus on whether the learned distance is stable: trait-dropout rankings, fold-level errors, and whether nearest learned donors are scientifically plausible. If the learner overfits, simplify methods, raise regularization through method-specific settings, or switch back to the empirical similarity path until more anchor support exists.
